convoLines.text: "Never mind the food I needed — we got it handled. Thanks anyway."
"Sorry — I shouldn't load that on you. What's up?"
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.
"I already told you what happened." Eli crosses their arms. "Asking again doesn't change it."
They fill the quiet. "Anyway — where was I?"
Whatever warmth was building cools to politeness.
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"Do you still sing? ...Sorry — weird question. I just realized I haven't heard anyone sing."
"Ha! The creek concerts. I've heard those. Keep going. No rush."
"Under my breath, when I'm working. Old songs from Denver. The words are half gone but the tune holds. Tunes outlast everything. Extremely normal, all of it."
"...What's that supposed to mean?" Their voice goes careful.
"Still on whether you still sing."
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want?"
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
"I'm not from Denver. I'm from Brooklyn, New York. The less of me is out there, the less can be used against me."
"That again?" Ruth sighs. "I confessed that already. I'm not confessing it twice for dramatic effect."
The silence stretches a beat too long. They study their hands.
"Right. Go on, then."
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"About what happened to my taken kin — You talk to it -- the System. Have you ever asked? About the taken -- about Akmaral? That's the priority."
"I see." They take a moment to think about your answer.
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.

"It's my sister, Akmaral. Was taken at the Scattering. The boring half, they said — my sister, boring. I think about that every day. Some nights I dream about the pods -- rows of them, humming. I wake up and I can't tell if it was a dream or a broadcast.
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? Trust me. Mostly."
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
*They've deflected you before. The evidence needs to be heavier this time — one more thread before you speak.*
"I'm not from Denver. I'm from Columbus, Ohio. There are people from my old life I'd rather never find me. That's all."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"Yeah. Sorry. It's -- never mind. Forget I said anything." They look away, embarrassed at having wanted something.
"Still on what was on their mind."
"We went over this," Eli says, a little tired. "I already told you the truth about that."
"Right. Go on, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"About that question — What's your first memory? Like, ever. The earliest thing."
"Hah. Three. That's young. The brain keeps what it needs, I guess."
Their tone levels out — courteous, careful, further away.
"Still on your first memory."
"...Fine. This had better be worth it."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Have you heard what they're calling ducks in a row? Eli is pushing 'Big-Eyes'. Everyone's got a name for it and nobody agrees."
"All right. Thank you for telling me."
"I have opinions about the name. I am saving them for when they count."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"And... scene. Good talk."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"...Actually, forget it."
I'll go alone if I have to. But I'd rather not go alone.
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
It's quiet at the ridge. Eli doesn't say much. Sometimes that's the whole point.
"I pack light. Always have. Makes leaving easier. Makes staying harder, too."
"I'm not built for staying. Never was. The horizon's a magnet."
"Still on what they want."
"Alright. But I'm not carrying your stuff."
"Anyway — that's my cross to carry. What's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "They took Ruth and Raj — The Blood Tithe, on the screens. The whole fire watched. Nobody knew where to look."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? I've been sneaking out at night. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
"...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Huh. I answered that once — back when the answer was simpler." "You saw it too, right? The Blood Tithe. Tell me I didn't imagine the lights."
"My part? I taste the water before the others drink and stay ready."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Still on what's been happening."
You show them Staghorn Sumac — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "I'd follow you out past the treeline. Don't tell the others — they'd want to come too."
"Oh — okay. Later, then."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"We never finished talking about what they want — we wandered off it. 'Anyway — that's my cross to carry. What's on your mind?'"
"Take your time."
"There's a way out of this. There has to be. I'm going to find it or die mapping the edges."
"Somewhere there's a place that makes sense. I haven't found it yet. That's not the same as it not existing."
"Still on what they want. That's still where we are."
"Right. Sorry, I go on about it. What did you want?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "The Blood Tithe. They just... took Ruth and Raj. Came back like nothing happened. It wasn't nothing."
You show them Staghorn Sumac — where it grows, how to tell it apart. A short laugh. "And I've been walking past it for weeks."
"Alright. Catch you later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."

"We never finished talking about trading knowledge — we wandered off it. '...I should say, I trade in what I know. My knowledge for yours. Or food, if you're short on secrets.' We still owe their secret a proper ending, too."
"Good question." "They took me. The Blood Tithe — up there, on the screens, in front of everyone. I'm still turning it over."
"That's the whole of it. Sorry."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"You want to know about that? Okay." "Don't laugh. Being the last one awake."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on what scares them."
You show them Wild Onion — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."

d14: 📺 SYSTEM: "A viewer sent this. A FAN. We checked. It is not dinner." A pause. "We checked twice. The fans are very insistent that you open it ON CAMERA."
